body.heading: Make it sing
paragraphs: Lay a ruler on a table so that half of it sticks out over the edge. Press down hard on the part on the table and flick the free end.
The ruler bounces up and down very fast and sings a low, funny note. That fast bouncing is called vibration, and vibration is what sound is made of.

body.heading: Short and long
paragraphs: Slide the ruler so only a little sticks out, and flick it again. Now the note is higher and the bounce is faster and smaller.
Long overhang, slow vibration, low sound. Short overhang, fast vibration, high sound. You have just played physics.

body.heading: See the sound
paragraphs: Watch the ruler's end closely as it sings. At first it is a blur. As the sound fades, you can see the bouncing slow down and stop.
Guitars, drums, and your own voice all work by vibrating. The twanging ruler is their table-top cousin.

takeaway: Sound is vibration — a long ruler vibrates slowly with a low note, and a short one vibrates fast and high.
safetyNotes: Hold the ruler firmly so it does not fly off the table. Keep faces away from the twanging end.
screenFreeExtension: Make a family orchestra of twangs — long rulers sing low, short rulers sing high.
